judged_text: updateEvent's fallback event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it searches for a calendar whose externalId equals that falsy value and always returns undefined - the review-base fallback to destinationCalendar.externalId is now dead code. Every booking that has a destination calendar but whose BookingReference lacks externalCalendarId (legacy destination calendars without credentialId, whose fan-out path passes no externalId, plus pre-refactor references) fails to reschedule or edit: calendar.events.update is called with an undefined required calendarId, the Google client rejects it, and the external calendar event keeps the old time while Cal.com shows the new one.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the `updateEvent` fallback logic is incorrect: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (null/undefined), the code executes the `.find(...)` branch but compares each `cal.externalId` to that same falsy `externalCalendarId`, so it will almost always return `undefined`. Unlike `createEvent`, there is no `|| "primary"` fallback in `updateEvent`, so `calendar.events.update` can be invoked with an undefined `calendarId`, breaking updates for cases where references don't provide `externalCalendarId`.
